subject: Determining significance with categorical predictors of abundance in pcount

messages.author: c27b5a30c13a701e
messages.subject: Determining significance with categorical predictors of abundance in pcount
parts:
Hello all,

Apologies if this has an obvious answer, but I've been searching and can't find one. If you have a categorical predictor for abundance in pcount (let's say for example, urban, suburban, or rural) and run the model, if will spit out a GLM-style set of p-values, but I don't see any way to do post-hoc contrasts, like a Tukey's for example, to see if your categories are significantly different from each other.

I did try running modavgPred with parm.type = "lambda", type = "response", and then setting c.hat as determined by the gof test (Nmix.gof.test), using "new data" that sets everything else the same but the categorical variable of interest. I then compare the upper and lower confidence limits of the predicted data to check for overlap between the categories. Is this a valid/correct approach? Or should I just be comparing the p-values, or is there a post-hoc Tukey-style test for N-mixture models that I'm just missing?

Thank you all!

-Aaron

messages.author: 4e956cc50ac3e075
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Determining significance with categorical predictors of abundance in pcount
parts:
Hi Aaron,

There are a few options available. For example, you could use
orthogonal contrasts to combine and compare groups of interest (same
type used in classic ANOVA). Computing predictions for each group as
you have done and plotting confidence intervals is another option,
although you have to be careful about the interpretation of the degree
of overlap between intervals (check Cumming, G. 2009. Inference by eye:
reading the overlap of independent confidence intervals. Statistics in
Medicine 28:205-220.). A third option is to compare two groups of
interest using modavgEffect( ) in AICcmodavg, where you create a
newdata data frame which has two rows (1 for each group of interest)
and compute a confidence interval around the difference in groups.

Best,

Marc

messages.author: 247b990d236a7af6
messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Determining significance with categorical predictors of abundance in pcount
parts:
You can use a "brute-force" approach as follows (slightly modifying the mallard example in the documentation for pcount):

# Load library
  library(unmarked)

# Get data
  data(mallard)
 
# Add in categorical land use variable
  n <- length(mallard.site[,1])
  mallard.site$LandUse = factor(c(rep("Urban",floor(n/4)), rep("Suburban", floor(n/4)),
    rep("Rural", n-2*floor(n/4))))
  mallardUMF <- unmarkedFramePCount(mallard.y, siteCovs = mallard.site,
    obsCovs = mallard.obs)

# Run analysis
  (fm.mallard <- pcount(~ ivel + date + I(date^2) ~ 0 + LandUse + length + elev + forest,
    mallardUMF, K=30))

# Get estimates of parameters and covariance matrix
  (estimates = fm.mallard@estimates@estimates$state@estimates[1:3])
  (covmat = fm.mallard@estimates@estimates$state@covMat[1:3,1:3])
 
# List desired comparisons (linear combinations in this case)
# U for Urban, S for Suburban, and R for Rural.
  UvsS <- c(1, -1, 0)
  UvsR <- c(1, 0, -1)
  SvsR <- c(0, 1, -1)
 
# Estimates of differences
  UvsS.estimate <- UvsS %*% estimates
  UvsR.estimate <- UvsR %*% estimates
  SvsR.estimate <- SvsR %*% estimates
 
# Estimates of standard errors
  UvsS.se <- (UvsS %*% covmat %*% UvsS)^0.5
  UvsR.se <- (UvsR %*% covmat %*% UvsR)^0.5
  SvsR.se <- (SvsR %*% covmat %*% SvsR)^0.5
   
# z-statistics
  (UvsS.z <- UvsS.estimate/UvsS.se)
  # [1,] 1.616347
  (UvsR.z <- UvsR.estimate/UvsR.se)
  # [1,] 0.470982
  (SvsR.z <- SvsR.estimate/SvsR.se)
  # [1,] -1.157075

You can then decide on how or if you want to adjust for multiple comparisons.

Jim
